challenge.better_approach: Considered two: (a) fallback only when no test_ line printed — measured false, 32 mixed seals carry real label teeth; (b) change the cc printer — 8f5ab45e64c5 adjudicated that the printer is left alone and the parser never invents a red. Narrowing the fallback's vocabulary to the measured report tokens is the smallest change that keeps every real tooth.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the corpus on akiendelllinux today is representative of what proofs print. A red seal is rarer than a green one, so red-vocabulary label teeth are under-sampled (RED n=2). Mitigation: 'fail' stays in the narrowed set because the tester's own printer emits FAIL (proof_coverage.py:937, 979).
challenge.prior_art: 8e2018855b31 (PROVED) and 8f5ab45e64c5 fixed the path-label instance only (_PATH_LABEL). Congruency lab grepped for _MARKER_LABEL/label fallback: no other intention. ddc5cb6694d3/d845546b67b9 add a NOTRUN marker — a distinct word, no collision, but whoever builds second must keep NOTRUN in the label vocabulary if it reaches the fallback.
challenge.real_collision: None exclusive. Distinction: the label fallback stops reading 'failed/error/errored/broken/passed/good' as markers; a proof that wants those words to mark a tooth must name it with test_ (the anchored patterns still read them).

answers.falsifier: (1) the cc seal's stdout above parses to its 4 test_ teeth green and 0 red; (2) every label tooth the corpus parses today under ok/pass/green/red/fail parses identically after the change (same green and red lists for all 900 seals except the cc one); (3) test_NO_GREEN_SEAL_IN_THE_CORPUS_PARSES_TO_A_RED_TOOTH is green over the whole corpus. WRONG INTENT if a proof in the corpus prints a real red tooth by label under 'failed', 'error', 'errored' or 'broken' — then the vocabulary is the wrong discriminator.
answers.from_idea: none, because this is a measured false red, not an idea: cairn/devices/cc/validations/test_a_close_over_a_diverged_repo_rebases_or_stops.json is verdict green with teeth_red ['pull: rc 5, named, no crossing, 1 ahead, no rebase left open'], found by akiendelllinux_cc_0 walking FIXME ae0d88a55edb on 2026-11-22
answers.how: Measured 2026-11-22 over every validation's stdout_tail (900 seals with teeth): lines that reach the label fallback (_MARKER_LABEL, proof_coverage.py:93) carry exactly these marker words: ok 454, PASS 452+28, green 301+5, GREEN 27+18, pass 18, RED 2 (in red seals) — and two data rows: 'failed pull: rc 5 ...' (cc, green seal) and 'red  /var/tmp/...' (tester, already refused by _PATH_LABEL, 8e2018855b31). So the label fallback reads its marker from a narrower set, the report tokens {ok, pass, green, red, fail} folded; the test_-anchored patterns (_MARKER_FIRST/_MARKER_LAST) keep the full GREEN_MARKERS/RED_MARKERS vocabulary unchanged. A first idea, 'skip the fallback when a proof prints any test_ tooth', was measured false: 32 seals mix test_ teeth with real label teeth (e.g. test_exemption_set.json 'ok   an absent set reds').
answers.traces_to: Law 8 and Law 9: a false red at the PROVED gate is distance the proof never reported; 8e2018855b31's tooth states the invariant 'the parser never invents a red from a green proof's printed data', and it still breaks for any red-vocabulary word opening a data row. Law 1: fix the class, not the next instance.
answers.what: proof_coverage's label fallback mints a tooth only from the report words proofs actually print as tooth markers, so a green proof's indented data row that opens with a word like 'failed' is never read as a red tooth.

bullets.text: Measured: of 900 sealed proofs, 32 legitimately mix test_ teeth with label teeth, so 'ignore labels when test_ teeth exist' would drop real teeth.
Measured: the only label-fallback reds in green seals are two data rows ('failed pull: ...' in cc, a /var/tmp path in tester); every real label tooth uses ok/pass/green/red.
